name: Darwinopterus
sum: Classic transitional pterosaur from the Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China, combining a pterodactyloid-like head and neck with a long ‘rhamphorhynchoid’ tail.
holotype: Type species D. modularis (Lü et al. 2010) — Tiaojishan Formation, Linglongta, Jianchang, Liaoning.
material: 30–40 specimens, many complete skeletons; four species described, two of which have been argued to be junior synonyms of D. modularis (Zhou et al. 2021).
exceptional: The egg-bearing specimen ‘Mrs T’ (ZMNH M8802), first described as Darwinopterus, was reassigned to Kunpengopterus antipollicatus in 2021.
biology: Spike-like, widely spaced teeth; probably took small vertebrates and insects. Crests may relate to sex, though this is debated.
